legacy_root.answer: Quantified OA-measured effects: debate Du et al. GSM8K-100 85.0 ± 3.5 vs single-agent 77.0 ± 4.2 (independently contradicted: Zhang et al. MAD win rate vs CoT not higher than 20% across 36 scenarios; Smit et al. MAD does not reliably outperform self-consistency). Verifier-in-the-loop Cobbe et al. 6B verification slightly outperforms a finetuned 175B model (~30x size-equivalent); independently Lightman PRM solves 78.2% of a MATH subset at Best-of-1860. Best-of-n Lightman PRM 78.2 vs majority 69.6 at Best-of-1860 (Cobbe independently specifies sample-100 + rank). Self-consistency Wang et al. PaLM-540B GSM8K 74.4 (+17.9) from 56.5; Lightman majority 69.6 is an independent majority-vote measurement on MATH. Execution-consensus AlphaCode top 54.3% on Codeforces contests with >5000 participants (SINGLE-SOURCE). Role-committees MetaGPT Pass@1 85.9% / 87.7% vs GPT-4 HumanEval baseline 67% (SINGLE-SOURCE). Delphi: UNQUANTIFIED (OA full text not held; no paraphrased percent). Estate IMPLEMENTED: 1 protocol(s) delphi->CNL-0035. Do not rebuild an IMPLEMENTED protocol under a new id.

non_equivalent.why: Matched-pair negotiation with a voteless mediator, not multi-agent debate with shared-context rebuttal rounds.

independent_signals.quote: none of these MAD methods achieve a win rate higher than 20% when compared to CoT across 36 scenarios (4 models × 9 benchmarks)
independent_signals.title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity

independent_signals.quote: multi-agent debating systems, in their current form, do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies, such as self-consistency and ensembling using multiple reasoning paths
independent_signals.reported_value: do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies, such as self-consistency
independent_signals.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs

negative_hunt.note: Hunt used negative phrasing. Du et al. is one confirmatory signal; Smit et al. and Zhang et al. are independent and contradict a general 'debate beats a single well-prompted model' claim.
queries: multi-agent debate does not outperform chain-of-thought

primary.anchor: Table 1, Multi-Agent (Debate) row, Grade School Math column
primary.authors: Du, Yilun; Li, Shuang; Torralba, Antonio; Tenenbaum, Joshua B.; Mordatch, Igor
primary.dataset: GSM8K (100-problem subset; Grade School Math column of Table 1)
primary.quote: Table 1: Multiagent Debate Improves Reasoning Multi-agent debate improves the reasoning abilities of language models. Multi-agent results in the table are run with 3 agents and two rounds of debate. | Single Agent | 67.0 ± 4.7 | 77.0 ± 4.2 | 91.4 ± 10.6 | | Multi-Agent (Debate) | 81.8 ± 2.3 | 85.0 ± 3.5 | 122.9 ± 7.6 |
primary.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate

negative_hunt.note: Secondary abstracts report mixed findings: Delphi often beats unstructured groups but is not consistently superior to other structured procedures. No OA numeric delta copied.
queries: Delphi no more accurate than unstructured interacting groups
Delphi herding accuracy worse across rounds

protocols.settling_experiment: Obtain OA or licensed full text of Rowe & Wright 1999 (or Dalkey RAND RM-5888) and copy one verbatim accuracy/round table cell; until then Delphi remains UNQUANTIFIED, not a paraphrased percent.

independent_signals.quote: We use our state-of-the-art PRM to solve 78.2% of problems from a representative subset of the MATH test set.

negative_hunt.note: Lightman et al. also report majority voting at 69.6% vs PRM 78.2% at Best-of-1860 — majority is weaker, not a null of verification. Gao et al. document BoN overoptimization as the failure mode when the reward model is exploited.
queries: verifier reward model overoptimization best-of-n fails
process supervision does not outperform outcome supervision
